rule: Built by scripts/build_innovator_report.py for the Innovator Market Analysis Report (app/innovator-report.js). Holds only what that report cannot read in the browser: the award history of each speciality's competitor set, reduced from data/company-awards.json (20 MB); the Stakeholder Mapper's role library, parsed from app/mst-logic.js; a digital flag on the other-body framework rows; and every source file's own as-of date, so an unreachable source can still be reported with its last good reading. Nothing here is computed beyond counts, earliest and latest dates, and a name match.
matchRule: A competitor row is tied to a company in company-awards.json by the normalised form of its `ref` (the master supplier record), falling back to its `co`. Where no company matches, the row is written with awardCount 0 and matched false, and the report prints "No award row in the Hub's set" — which is not the same as "no contracts", and the report says so.
digitalRule: A row is flagged digital when its own name appears in the explicit list in scripts/build_innovator_report.py (DIGITAL_ROWS), each of which was read at its own agreement page. No keyword match is used: a keyword match would catch a framework for digital thermometers and miss one named only for its service.
frameworkMatchRule: A speciality's NHS Supply Chain framework rows are the rows in frameworks.json whose own `name` appears inside one of the framework names in that speciality's curated route in compare-suppliers.json. Longest name first, so "General Wound Care" is not swallowed by "Wound Care". Each row keeps its own Contract Launch Brief URL, and carries the renewal signals from framework-directory-extra.json and the NHS Supply Chain procurement-calendar rows that name it.
tenderSlugRule: The open-tenders.json speciality slug for a speciality is reached in two hops through products.json, both of them the Hub's own: the speciality's EVIDENCE_BAND, then that band's own progress_slug in EVIDENCE_HIGHLIGHTS. A speciality with no band has no slug and the report says the tender feed cannot be filtered for it, rather than guessing a slug.
digitalArmRule: For a software or diagnostic-software product the route comes from digital-frameworks.json (ten agreements read at their own GCA, NHS SBS and Find a Tender pages) and the competitor set from company-digital-awards.json (companies that have won a digital NHS award). The framework lots' supplier lists are deliberately NOT carried into the report: Technology Services 4 Lot 1 alone names hundreds of IT suppliers, almost none of them health tech, so printing that list as "who already sells here" would be a false competitor set. Each lot's supplier count and its own page URL are shown instead.

company-awards.json.source: Find a Tender and Contracts Finder award-stage OCDS notices, Open Government Licence v3 — the weekly walk of both feeds, plus the award history of the same two feeds, held as the Hub's tender and award history

compare-suppliers.json.sourceRule: Every framework name, its dates and its supplier list come from that framework's own contract launch brief on supplychain.nhs.uk, fetched directly. Brand names come from the NHS Supply Chain online catalogue entry for the supplier's own NPC codes — the procurement record, not the supplier's marketing. Nothing here is inferred from a trade summary or a comparison table.

frameworks.json.source: NHS Supply Chain Contract Launch Briefs (https://www.supplychain.nhs.uk/product-information/contract-launch-briefs/), each framework's own page, fetched this run.

framework-directory-extra.json.checkedAt: 20 of 23 rows re-read at their source by scripts/check_other_body_frameworks.py, 12/11/2026; 17 digital and technology rows added 16/11/2026, each read at its own agreement page that day (NHS SBS 'What dates is the framework agreement active?' line; GCA agreement pages)
framework-directory-extra.json.rule: Curated, source-linked additions to the Frameworks directory on Hub page 3198. The page renders NHS Supply Chain frameworks live from frameworks.json (Contract Launch Briefs, weekly) and their next tender from nhssc-procurement-calendar.json (daily). This file holds only what those two cannot: frameworks run by other bodies, and one-off signals read at a named source. Every entry was checked at its source on the date given. The page hides any framework whose end date has passed, so a stale row drops off rather than showing as live.

open-tenders.json.source: Find a Tender and Contracts Finder tender-stage OCDS notices, Open Government Licence v3

pending-awards.json.source: Find a Tender award-stage OCDS notices naming Supply Chain Coordination Limited (NHS Supply Chain's own legal buyer name) as buyer, with a framework agreement. Open Government Licence v3. https://www.find-tender.service.gov.uk/

digital-frameworks.json.source: gca.gov.uk agreement pages and lot-supplier CSV exports; find-tender.service.gov.uk OCDS API; sbs.nhs.uk framework pages
digital-frameworks.json.rule: Every fact read at the named primary source on verifiedOn, else 'Not verified' with what would settle it. Supplier lists hold company names only; no contact person, email, phone or address is ever stored. suppliers null means no list was read.

company-digital-awards.json.source: Find a Tender and Contracts Finder award notices in the Hub's digital lane (data/digital-lane.json), Open Government Licence v3.
company-digital-awards.json.laneRule: A Find a Tender or Contracts Finder notice is in this lane when the buyer name is an NHS body (contains "NHS", "Integrated Care Board" or "Health Board"; bare "Trust" is not a match) AND a Common Procurement Vocabulary (CPV) code on the notice begins 48 (software package and information systems) or 72 (IT services). An Atamis opportunity carries no CPV code, so its own Category text stands in: a software, information systems or IT services category, or a title naming a clinical digital system. Every Atamis authority is an NHS body by construction.

nhssc-procurement-calendar.json.source: NHS Supply Chain, procurement calendar page, as fetched by scripts/refresh_nhssc_procurement_calendar.py

products.json.note: The Hub's own speciality list, product and problem list, framework family map, national priority map and Clinical Evidence Library highlights — the same records behind the Hub's Stakeholder Mapper and Value Equation. Human-curated; no automation writes it.

app/mst-logic.js.note: The Hub's Stakeholder Mapper. Its role library is read straight out of the tool, so the roles in this report and the roles a member sees in the mapper cannot drift apart.

payer.whoPri: ICB finance and commissioning (community / prescribing budget)
payer.cares: Cash-releasing savings, capacity, length of stay, CQC position
payer.evidence: A banked, attributable business case plus local baseline audit
payer.hook: Reduce the problem with a saving you can point to and bank

decision_maker.whoSec: Clinical lead plus procurement / product evaluation group
decision_maker.whoPri: ICB formulary and service lead; PCN clinical directors
decision_maker.cares: Evidence quality, framework / formulary compliance, total cost of ownership
decision_maker.evidence: Peer-reviewed data, framework/formulary availability, NICE/GIRFT alignment
decision_maker.hook: Evidence-backed, compliant-route, low-risk swap that moves a measured KPI
decision_maker.risk: Will require a local pilot and a compliant route before sign-off

user.whoPri: GPs, practice and community / district nurses
user.cares: Ease of use, time, safety, fewer failures, patient experience
user.evidence: Acceptability / ease-of-use data and a simple training plan
user.hook: Easier, safer, right-first-time without extra steps
user.risk: Will abandon anything that adds steps, training burden or fails in use

ipc.cares: Infection rates, diagnostic and antimicrobial stewardship, CQC IPC assurance
ipc.hook: Fewer infections / false positives, a stewardship and assurance win
ipc.risk: Influential blocker or champion; ignore them and adoption stalls

microbiology.cares: Avoidable repeat tests, lab capacity, turnaround, cost per test
microbiology.evidence: Local repeat-rate audit plus lab cost modelling
microbiology.hook: Fewer avoidable repeats equals released lab capacity and faster turnaround
microbiology.risk: Holds the data that proves or sinks your case; engage early

stewardship.whoPri: ICB / PCN prescribing and AMR lead
stewardship.evidence: Link between the problem and unnecessary prescribing; stewardship outcomes
stewardship.hook: Fewer false positives directly supports your AMR targets
stewardship.risk: A credibility multiplier; their endorsement de-risks the case

sharps.whoSec: Sharps safety / health and safety committee
sharps.cares: Needlestick injuries, staff safety, sharps regulations compliance
sharps.evidence: Incident-rate data and safety-engineered device evidence
sharps.hook: Fewer needlestick incidents, safer staff and regulatory compliance
sharps.risk: Safety mandate can accelerate adoption, or block a non-compliant device

procurement.whoSec: Category manager for YOUR speciality (not the department)
procurement.cares: Price, framework compliance, total cost, maverick-spend control
procurement.evidence: Framework position, price benchmarking, total cost of ownership
procurement.hook: A compliant, better-value route that fits your category plan
procurement.risk: Off-framework or poor-value routes get rejected regardless of clinical merit

tissue_viability.cares: Healing rates, avoidable pressure / wound harm, nurse-visit burden
tissue_viability.hook: Faster healing equals fewer visits, shorter stays, less avoidable harm
tissue_viability.risk: Owns the harm metrics; a key clinical gatekeeper for wound/skin products

ebme.cares: Maintenance, training, uptime, servicing (incl. LOLER), capital fit
ebme.evidence: Servicing/maintenance profile, training need, uptime data
ebme.hook: Lower servicing burden and reliable uptime for your team
ebme.risk: Can veto on maintenance, safety or interoperability grounds

decontamination.cares: Reprocessing load, compliance (JAG / HTM), capacity, traceability
decontamination.evidence: Reprocessing volumes, compliance position, capacity modelling
decontamination.hook: Less reprocessing equals more throughput and easier compliance
decontamination.risk: Compliance failures here stop a whole service; engage early

sustainability.cares: Carbon footprint, waste, net-zero targets, single-use vs reusable
sustainability.evidence: Carbon / waste data and net-zero alignment
sustainability.hook: A lower-carbon option that performs and supports your Green Plan
sustainability.risk: Sustainability is now a scored procurement criterion; ignore at your cost

medicines.cares: Formulary choice, prescribing spend, variation, adherence
medicines.hook: A better-value, formulary-ready option that cuts downstream cost
medicines.risk: Formulary gatekeeping; no formulary place, no volume

dietitian.cares: Malnutrition risk, feed safety, ONS prescribing spend, MUST scores
dietitian.hook: Better nutrition outcomes with controlled feed / ONS spend
dietitian.risk: Owns the nutrition pathway; a key clinical gatekeeper

radiation_protection.whoSec: Radiation protection adviser / medical physics expert
radiation_protection.cares: Patient and staff dose, IR(ME)R compliance, QA, safety
radiation_protection.hook: Lower dose and easier IR(ME)R compliance
radiation_protection.risk: Can block on radiation-safety or compliance grounds

pharmacy.cares: Medicines safety, aseptic capacity, drug budget, governance
pharmacy.hook: A safer, more efficient medicines / aseptic pathway
pharmacy.risk: Governs medicines and aseptic prep; gatekeeper for SACT / PN

manual_handling.whoSec: Manual handling lead / back care adviser (moving and handling team, health and safety, or therapies)
manual_handling.whoPri: Community moving and handling lead / trainer
manual_handling.cares: Staff musculoskeletal injury and sickness absence, MHOR risk assessment, staff competence and training, safe working load and equipment compatibility
manual_handling.evidence: Risk-assessment evidence: reduction in handling force or number of handlers, staff injury and sickness data, training and competence requirements
manual_handling.hook: Fewer handling injuries, fewer staff off sick, and a risk assessment that stands up
manual_handling.risk: Approach this role FIRST. Nothing in patient handling is adopted against the manual handling lead, and going to procurement or the ward ahead of them is the classic way to lose the account.

patient.cares: Dignity, safety, right-first-time care, fewer repeat visits, avoided harm
patient.hook: A dignified, accurate, less burdensome experience
patient.risk: Experience and harm drive complaints, PALS and CQC scrutiny

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Respiratory Solutions (6 lots, 37 suppliers). Lot 5 is Diagnostics

respiratory.routeNote: Six lots: oxygen therapy, aerosol therapy, respiratory therapy, anaesthesia and resuscitation, diagnostics, and sterile water for humidification. Incentive spirometers are ward-level respiratory therapy — the people who feel a shortage are physiotherapy and enhanced recovery, not procurement. More companies from the Hub's verified supplier index are listed below without catalogue-level product detail yet (marked as such in their row) — added 02/09/2026 from the index the Hub already held, not fresh research.

frameworks.name: Respiratory Solutions
suppliers: Mediq Healthcare Uk Limited Ex Bunzl Hea
frameworks.supplierSource: no stated count on the page; 37 names parsed (UNVERIFIED COUNT)

lotTitles.Lot 1: Oxygen Therapy – includes oxygen facemask and nebuliser
lotTitles.Lot 3: Respiratory Therapy – include spirometers, peak flow meters, cough assist devices and compressor nebuliser
lotTitles.Lot 4: Anaesthesia and Resuscitation – includes anaesthetic facemasks, absorbers and corrugated tubing, plus bag valve mask, mannequins and CPR masks
lotTitles.Lot 5: Diagnostics – this is a new lot which has been developed in conjunction with respiratory specialists to support ease of procurement both supplier and clinical
lotTitles.Lot 6: Sterile Water for humidification – includes sterile water used for humidification

route.note: Capital equipment — tables, lights, OR integration systems, sterilizers and their accessories — bought Direct rather than off a lotted catalogue. theatres.routeNote: Four routes, because theatres is not one buying line. Surgical gloves is a single lot with nine suppliers. Electrosurgical Consumables (which replaced the old Diathermy Consumables framework) runs six lots: diathermy plates, pencils, smoke evacuation, argon pencils, suction coagulators and forceps. Patient Temperature Management runs five lots covering forced air warming, blood and fluid warming, temperature equipment, passive warming and sensors — and NHS Supply Chain has said it is renewing that one for a mid-2027 launch, so it is the one to watch. Operating Theatres Equipment is the capital route — tables, lights and OR integration systems, bought Direct rather than as a stock catalogue line. route.note: Basic dressings, bandages, tapes, plasters and first aid — the separate framework the Advanced Wound Care routeNote already pointed at. Crest Medical Ltd is named on this award list. Added 19/08/2026 after 872 of Crest Medical's crawled divisions (workplace, motorist and travel first aid kits, plasters, crepe and triangular bandages, eye pads, ambulance dressings, saline wound-cleansing spray) turned up with nowhere to go in the four Advanced Wound Care types.

wound.routeNote: Eighteen lots covering hydrogels, gelling fibres and alginates, wound contact layers, super absorbents, foams, hydrocolloids, IV and film dressings, burns and scar management, irrigation, debridement, adhesive removers, skin protectants, compression bandages and adhesive tapes. Developed with clinicians and aligned to the National Wound Care Strategy Programme. General wound care sits on its own separate framework, and wound closure and negative pressure wound therapy sit on two more again — check which one a product is actually on before quoting a route. route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Endoscopy, Endourology and Oncology Ablation Consumables and Associated Products (3 lots, 58 suppliers, 17 of them new)

endoscopy.routeNote: Three lots: endoscopy, endourology and oncology ablation. Consumables only — the scopes themselves and the washer-disinfectors that reprocess them are bought on separate frameworks, and decontamination capital is under Sterile services here. A trust's endoscopy unit therefore buys from three different routes, which is worth knowing before you promise to 'sort endoscopy' for them. imaging.routeNote: CT only, and only eight suppliers — one of the most concentrated fields in this tool. Six categories: general, advanced and premium CT, wide-bore for radiotherapy simulation, and mobile scanners for head-and-neck or whole-body. Every other imaging modality is bought on its own separate framework (MRI, bone densitometers, contrast injectors, angiography and hybrid theatres, digital diagnostics), so check which one a product is actually on before quoting a route. This is capital with a long service tail — the sale is an estate and business-case conversation, not a consumable one. More companies from the Hub's verified supplier index are listed below without catalogue-level product detail yet (marked as such in their row) — added 02/09/2026 from the index the Hub already held, not fresh research. `inject` added 20/09/2026 under the identity policy table's vocabulary-gap policy (add-only standing authority). Prompted by Medical Imaging Systems (MIS Healthcare)'s four Nemoto contrast injectors (CT Dual Shot Alpha 7, Smart Shot Alpha, MRI Sonic Shot 7, Press Duo Elite) and HC21 (UK) Ltd's Optivantage Multiuse, none of which had a home: an injector is not a scanner, so filing it under imaging:ct or imaging:mri would publish a contrast pump into a scanner comparison. Name taken from MIS Healthcare's own 'Injectors' sub-category and HC21's own 'CT Injectors' division. Two suppliers populate it, so it is not a type invented for one odd product.

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Maternity, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Sexual Health Products (2 lots, 54 suppliers, 11 of them new)

womens.routeNote: Two lots: Lot 1 Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Maternity, and Lot 2 Sexual Health. It merges what used to be two separate frameworks, so a supplier who only ever sold into maternity now sits on the same agreement as the sexual health suppliers. The products are used on maternity and gynaecology wards, in theatres and outpatients, and in sexual health and GP clinics — four different buyers on one route. NHS Supply Chain publishes a single framework-wide supplier list and does not say who is awarded on which lot, so no lot membership is claimed here. Foetal monitoring belts and scalp electrodes are bought on the electrodes framework, and breast prostheses on their own — so check which route a product is actually on. Alarm monitoring (Lot 3) is the one growing, driven by alarm fatigue and deteriorating-patient work. handling.label: Patient handling and pressure area care

route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Pressure Area Care and Patient Handling (53 suppliers), reference 2025/S 000-086469, Rehabilitation and Community

handling.routeNote: Supply routes on this framework are Direct, Stocked and eDirect, so the same supplier can reach a trust three different ways and the route decides who signs. All 53 suppliers named on the brief are represented below. Eight carry catalogue-level evidence with NPC codes in each note (Arjo, Invacare, Etac, GBUK Healthcare, Direct Healthcare Group, Linet, Accora, Drive DeVilbiss); most of the rest carry product detail sourced from the supplier's own site — read each row's note for its actual source and date. A handful are named on the framework but have no confirmed patient-handling or pressure-area-care product on their own site (Agile Medical, Croyde Medical, Delta Surgical, Inspire Community Trust, Interweave Textiles, Medserve (South West), Mölnlycke, Peacocks Medical Group, Performance Health, Promedics) — shown honestly as such rather than padded, per the Hub's evidence rule. Bed frames — hospital, community and bariatric profiling beds — are bought on this same framework alongside the mattresses that sit on them. Companies beyond the 53-supplier roster (e.g. Vivid Care, CareFlex, Otto Bock, Baxter/Hillrom) sell direct off-framework or hold other framework positions and are included from the Hub's verified supplier index, marked as such in their own row. A duplicate row for 'Herida Healthcare' was removed 12/09/2026 — Winncare acquired and rebranded it in 2022; see the Winncare UK row's own note. A second dedup pass (12/09/2026) removed two further duplicates found to be the same corporate group as an existing row — Millbrook Healthcare (same group as Ultimate Healthcare) and Harvest Healthcare/Oxford Healthcare (both now Prism Healthcare Group, same as Prism Medical UK) — and fixed two more wrong-speciality product copy-ins (Crest Medical, Otto Bock).

ostomy.routeNote: THIS IS A DIFFERENT ROUTE TO MARKET FROM THE REST OF THIS TAB, and selling it as if it were NHS Supply Chain will lose the account. There is no framework to win, no tender and no award: a product gets a Part IX listing, a patient is prescribed it, and the dispenser is reimbursed at the Tariff price. The decision sits with the stoma care nurse specialist and the patient, and the volume flows through dispensing appliance contractors, not a trust's procurement team. Prices below are the Drug Tariff reimbursement price in the August 2026 edition and change monthly. 68 suppliers hold Part IXC listings; the ten below are the largest by listing count, together covering 5,478 of the 8,223 listings. route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Insulin Pumps, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Products Contributing to the Delivery of Hybrid Closed Loop Pathways and Associated Products (12 suppliers), reference 2025/S 000-4043, supply route Direct

diabetes.routeNote: TWO ROUTES, AND THEY ARE NOT ALTERNATIVES. The NHS Supply Chain framework above is real and names 12 suppliers — Abbott, Advanced Therapeutics, Air Liquide Healthcare, Dexcom, Glooko, GlucoRX Technologies, Insulet, Medtronic, Medtrum, Novo Nordisk, Urathon and Ypsomed — but it is the access route for pumps and hybrid closed loop, not how the consumable volume transacts. Sensors, strips, lancets and pen needles are prescribed and reimbursed through Part IX. The Hub's own catalogue check has already recorded FreeStyle Libre 2 Plus and 3 Plus as “Drug Tariff Part IX prescription” and MiniMed 780G with Guardian CGM as “insulin pump/CGM via prescription” — none of them is an NHS Supply Chain catalogue line, so none has an NPC code to quote. The table below is the Part IX competitor set. Insulet, Medtronic, Ypsomed, Medtrum, Glooko, Air Liquide, Advanced Therapeutics and Urathon hold no Part IX listing of their own and so do not appear in it; they are on the framework, which is a different question from being on the Tariff. THE PRICES ARE DIRECTLY COMPARABLE and rarely are: every row in the `cgm` column is a sensor reimbursed at a published monthly price, so this is one of the few genuinely like-for-like price comparisons on this tab. It changes every month — re-read the current edition before quoting it. route.name: NHS Supply Chain — Surgical Instruments (50 awarded suppliers)

surgical.routeNote: Reusable stainless-steel hand instruments. NHS Supply Chain's Surgical Instruments framework (reference 2020/S 170-412524, supply route Direct, Stocked and eDirect) names 50 awarded suppliers. The table below shows the 8 that pass all three evidence tests: named on the award list, own website proved against the company registration number published on that site, and an instrument range actually read from their own catalogue — so the families listed are what each supplier demonstrably sells, not what it might sell. The other 42 are named on the framework but not listed here: 29 have no verified website on record and 13 have a verified website but no instrument range read from it, and neither is a reason to send a rep to a page chosen on a guess. Reconcile against the framework total of 50; this table grows as those are proved. Single-use instrument ranges are deliberately excluded — they are theatre consumables and sit under Theatres, so a reusable instrument is never compared against a sterile single-use equivalent.
